methodological_rigor.justification: The study's core validation is largely circular: synthetic cohorts for AVM, VS, BM, and MEN are generated using pathology-specific logistic models of BED (Sections 2.3, 2.6.3, 2.7.3, 2.8.3), and then ML models are shown to recover the BED-driven relationships that were explicitly encoded. The Bayesian recovery of α/β = 2.47 (Section 3.1) is likewise obtained from data generated with that value, so it demonstrates identifiability under the model's own assumptions rather than clinical radiobiology. The only real-world comparison (Section 3.9) is a 60-lesion BM dataset lacking BED, time structure, or fractionation detail, so it cannot test the central AI-BED-Fx claim — it only shows that volume predicts recurrence. Statistical reporting is more careful (bootstrap 95% CIs, 5-fold CV with AUC 0.871 ± 0.069, hyperparameter grid search, cross-algorithm comparison, inter-fraction repair sensitivity analysis), but DeLong testing failed numerically (Section 2.11, 3.5.3), multiplicity across many pairwise model comparisons is not corrected, and no formal power analysis is reported.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is a mechanistic modeling / simulation study whose primary outputs derive from synthetic cohorts constructed with assumed radiobiological parameters, placing it at Oxford LoE 5. The 60-patient exploratory clinical check cannot validate BED, as the dataset lacks fractionation time structure and dosimetric detail (Section 3.9), and the authors themselves describe it as a 'sanity check' rather than validation. The clinical path is plausible — multi-fraction GKS BED modeling is a real gap — but no patient-relevant endpoints (OS, PFS, toxicity) are tested in actual patients, and no guideline or practice is directly informed. Translational relevance is thus speculative and contingent on future prospective validation that the manuscript explicitly defers.

reporting_quality.justification: TRIPOD is the closest fit because the work develops and internally evaluates multivariable prediction models (AUC/Brier, calibration curves, SHAP) across four pathologies, though the synthetic nature of training data makes several TRIPOD items (participants, missing data, Table 1 characteristics) only partially applicable. Methods for cohort generation, feature engineering, model training, bootstrap CIs, calibration, and SHAP are described in reasonable detail (Sections 2.4–2.11), and limitations are acknowledged. However, there is no mention of a public code repository, no data availability statement for the synthetic generators or the 60-patient clinical dataset, no protocol registration, no TRIPOD checklist, and no model-card-style reporting of hyperparameter search space, random seeds, or software versions beyond a brief listing.

novelty_literature.justification: The claimed novelty — a unified multi-fraction (1/3/5 fx) extension of the Jones–Hopewell biexponential-repair BED formalism coupled with an ML outcome layer and a neural-network surrogate — is a meaningful methodological extension of established work (Millar et al. [8], Jones & Hopewell [9]) rather than a conceptual breakthrough. The BED-vs-physical-dose pathology-dependent hierarchy (AVM > MEN > VS > BM) reproduces patterns already repeatedly documented in the empirical literature cited by the authors (Tuleasca, Nesvick, Shaaban, Zubatkina, Deng review [10–16]). The ML surrogate for BED and Bayesian α/β recovery are technically reasonable but demonstrated only on self-consistent synthetic data, which limits novelty of the empirical findings; the originality is primarily in packaging rather than new mechanistic insight or first-in-class empirical discovery.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is readable but suffers from severe redundancy and formatting artifacts: bulleted content is frequently duplicated (e.g., Section 2.5 Models A/B/C listed then re-listed, surrogate description repeated in 2.10, 'Fractionation Shifts' bullet fragmented in Section 3.2.5), equations are rendered inconsistently (e.g., Eq. 1, 7, 12 mix inline symbols and prose), and the Introduction/Discussion restate the same four take-home points multiple times. The abstract is quantitatively grounded and reasonably self-contained, but the paper is roughly 1.5–2× longer than needed because Section 3 recapitulates Section 2 and Section 4 recapitulates Section 3. Table captions and figure descriptions are present but table contents are often alluded to rather than shown, and several section headings (e.g., 2.8.6 'AI Perspective') read more as marketing than methods.

key_strengths: Addresses a genuine methodological gap: coherent multi-fraction (1/3/5 fx) extension of the Jones–Hopewell biexponential-repair BED formalism for Gamma Knife across four pathologies

Reasonably thorough internal evaluation: bootstrap 95% CIs, 5-fold CV, hyperparameter grid search, cross-algorithm comparison (XGBoost vs logistic vs RF), SHAP interpretability, and inter-fraction repair sensitivity analysis
Neural-network surrogate (R² = 0.9991, MAE 0.91 Gy) convincingly demonstrates that the BED mapping is learnable and could support differentiable optimization
Cross-pathology framing (AVM, MEN, VS, BM) is pedagogically useful and the pathology-dependent BED utility message is biologically coherent
key_concerns: Core validation is circular: ML models and the Bayesian α/β estimator recover relationships that were explicitly hard-coded into the synthetic generators (Sections 2.3, 2.6.3, 2.7.3, 2.8.3, 3.1), so claims of 'learning radiobiology from outcomes' are overstated

The only real-world comparison (60 BM lesions, Section 3.9) lacks fractionation time structure, dosimetry, and BED — it tests volume alone and cannot validate AI-BED-Fx; framing it as 'external face validity' is misleading
No data or code availability statement, no protocol registration, no checklist adherence; reproducibility rests entirely on the method prose

Severe writing redundancy and formatting artifacts (duplicated bullets, fragmented equations, repeated take-home messages across Introduction/Discussion/Conclusions) substantially inflate length and obscure the actual contribution
DeLong AUC comparison failed numerically (Section 2.11, 3.5.3) and no multiplicity correction is applied across the many pairwise model comparisons
Novelty is primarily methodological packaging; the pathology-dependent BED hierarchy and surrogate-ML concepts are already represented in the cited literature
chief_reviewer.rationale: The framework is interesting and internally competent, but the evidentiary structure is essentially self-confirmatory (synthetic data generated and recovered under the same assumptions) with only a non-informative 60-patient clinical anchor. Combined with reporting/reproducibility gaps and heavy writing redundancy, this is appropriate for a lower-tier methodological venue after major revisions that temper the 'learning radiobiology' claims and add genuine external validation plans or data.
